title: Plant Manager
text:
Chalk Point Generating Station, situated in Aquasco, Maryland, is a key power generation facility with a total capacity of approximately 1,618 MW. The station features a diverse lineup of nine generating units, including seven gas turbines and two steam turbines. This strategic configuration enhances efficiency and reliability, ensuring the station effectively meets regional energy demands.

**Opportunity Summary**

As the Plant Manager at Chalk Point Generating Station, you will oversee plant operations, maintenance, engineering, safety, environmental compliance, and administration to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective performance. Responsibilities include leading a union-represented workforce, managing budgets and contractual obligations, maintaining regulatory compliance, and driving operational improvements. Serving as the primary liaison between NAES and the Owner, you will also coordinate with regulatory agencies and community stakeholders to support facility objectives and maintain positive relationships.

***Your scope of responsibility as Plant Manager includes the following primary functions:***

* Direct plant operations, maintenance, safety, administrative, training, chemistry, NERC compliance, and environmental programs to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable performance while meeting operational targets.
* Oversee planned and forced outages, long-term maintenance planning, and asset reliability initiatives, optimizing schedules, resources, and contractor activities to minimize downtime and costs.
* Administer O&M, energy supply, service, and interconnection agreements while overseeing vendor performance and ensuring contractual compliance.
* Establish staffing, training, and qualification programs that support operational requirements, employee development, and facility objectives.
* Promote a strong safety culture through hazard identification, safe work practices, emergency preparedness, employee accountability, and adherence to established safety standards.
* Ensure environmental and regulatory compliance, including permits, landowner agreements, Management of Change (MOC) processes, and timely submission of required reports.
* Manage plant expenditures, operating and capital budgets, forecasting, procurement, and cost controls to achieve financial objectives and meet O&M Agreement requirements.
* Serve as the primary liaison with the Owner, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders, maintaining positive relationships and supporting community engagement.
* Monitor plant performance, reliability, and operating KPIs while supporting equipment troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions to improve operational efficiency.
* Lead union-represented and management personnel through performance management, collective bargaining agreement administration, labor relations, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational and workforce effectiveness.
* Maintain reliable attendance and availability to support facility operations and management responsibilities.

* Carry out and complete additional special projects and tasks as needed.

**NAES Safe**

Safety is a core value at NAES, and as a condition of employment, all employees are expected to remain mentally alert and work safely at all times. All NAES managers and supervisors have a direct and important role in ensuring that all work is performed in a healthy and safe manner. Effectiveness in carrying out this responsibility is part of the evaluation of each Supervisor’s performance.

**Working Relationships**

The Plant Manager reports to the Operations Director and supervises the managers, technicians, and Plant Administrator. The Plant Manager is the single point of contact between NAES and the Owner on all matters pertaining to the operation, maintenance, and commercial management of the plant.

**Physical Requirements and Working Conditions**

Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds.

Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions.

Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. Fit testing for respirators may be required. Strict smoking restrictions apply in and around the facility.

**Fitness for Duty**

All employees will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program. This program includes a post-offer physical examination and drug screening and post-employment random drug screening.

**Work Schedule**

The Plant Manager works a standard Monday to Friday day-shift schedule. This position will require extended hours, flexible shifts, weekends, and holidays as needed to support plant operations and business needs and may also require callout availability. Depending on the position, on-call status may or may not apply.

Some travel may be involved to participate in Manager, Owner, User Group, or other offsite meetings.

**Compensation**

This position offers an annual base salary ranging from $214,000 to $250,000 and includes eligibility for an annual performance bonus.

**Professional Experience and Leadership Competencies**

* A Bachelor of Science degree in engineering or equivalent is desired, providing a strong foundation for understanding the technical aspects of power plant operations and management.

* Previous Plant Manager experience at a gas- or oil-fired power generation facility, or comparable leadership experience overseeing similar industrial operations, is preferred.
* Proven experience supervising technical, supervisory, and union-represented personnel, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and labor relations.
* Extensive knowledge of power generation operations, independent power producer business practices, commercial agreements, and contractual requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in environmental and regulatory compliance, including applicable NERC requirements, operating and capital budgets, financial controls, and contract administration.
* Strong technical understanding of gas and steam turbine operations, outage management, equipment reliability, root cause analysis, and long-term maintenance planning.
* Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage employees, senior management, Owners, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Results-oriented approach to problem-solving, workforce development, emergency preparedness, change management, and continuous improvement across operational and financial functions.
* Must possess a valid, unrestricted U.S. driver’s license and ensure it remains in good standing at all times.

**About NAES**

NAES Corporation is a leading provider of operations, maintenance, and engineering services for energy facilities. We serve clients across the power generation, oil and gas, and renewable energy sectors throughout North America and internationally, supporting the full life cycle of power generation and other industrial facilities.

NAES is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on merit and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, military status, USERRA-protected status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
